title: Edge-favored routing with graceful capacity escrow
creator: Laura Chen
description: Design, prototype, and validate a routing policy that favors proximate (edge) regions while providing graceful capacity hedging via an escrowed token system to reduce hard shedding during regional overloads. This policy should: (1) prioritize p95/p99 latency SLOs, (2) respect customer geo-pinning preferences, (3) avoid cascading failures with multi-stage circuit breakers, and (4) enable progressive demotion to cheaper model variants when capacity is constrained.
background: We've seen two recurring failure modes: abrupt global shedding when a single region spikes, and excessive latency for pinned customers when naive geo-routing routes requests away from origin. Existing steerers either overprioritize latency (causing cold capacity misses) or over-shed aggressively. The proposed approach introduces a small region-local "capacity escrow" that temporarily absorbs burst demand and a multi-tier circuit breaker that uses probabilistic demotion instead of binary rejects.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end experiment showing a 40% reduction in immediate hard rejects during region overloads compared to current steerer. 2) P99 tail for edge-favored customers within 1.3x baseline for 99% of traffic. 3) No customer-pinned routes are violated without explicit override. 4) Operational dashboard surfaces escrow balance, demotion rates, and circuit breaker state with >= 1s update cadence.
design_notes:
Core concepts:
- Capacity escrow: allocate a small per-region token pool (default = 0.5% of steady-state QPS, min 10 tokens) that can be consumed to absorb short bursts. Tokens are refilled on a leaky-bucket basis tied to actual available headroom (not provisioned capacity).
- Steering score: weighted sum score = alpha * latency_score + beta * capacity_health + gamma * pin_score + delta * cost_pressure. alpha/beta/gamma tuned in traffic experiments.
- Circuit breakers: three tiers: (1) soft alarm (emit trace+metrics, reduce score to prefer local queueing), (2) probabilistic demote (N% of requests demoted to cheaper/quantized variant or downgraded model), (3) hard reject (token shedding) after demote threshold.
- Geo pinning: pin_score is additive large constant; but we allow a controlled soft-demote window for pinned traffic only when escrow tokens are exhausted and demotion rate hits cap. Pinned traffic should never be hard-rejected without an admin-level override.
- Observability: track per-region escrow_balance, refill_rate, consume_rate, demotion_rate, reject_rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies for primary and demoted path, and kv-cache hit ratio.
- Safety: global coordination uses an eventual consistency model with leaderless token gossip; proposals must avoid centralized coordinator for low latency.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Escrow reduces immediate rejects but increases cross-region hops if mis-sized, potentially raising overall latency and cost.
- Probabilistic demotion may surface quality regressions for some customers; need model-level A/B to measure quality delta.
- Leaderless escrow sync relies on approximate counts; risk of double-spending tokens across brief windows. Mitigation: per-request idempotency checks and short reservation leases.
- Complexity: adds more moving parts to the steering plane which increases operational burden. We'll run the feature behind a staged rollout and kill switch.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose leaky-bucket refill tied to observed headroom rather than static timer refill (decision by Michael).
2026-03-04: Agreed to cap demotion rate at 10% for non-pinned traffic and 3% for pinned traffic during experiments (PM/Eng consensus).
2026-03-08: Decided to persist escrow telemetry to a low-latency TSDB index for 7 days; aggregated rollups stored indefinitely (ops input).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (prototype): implement escrow bookkeeping, local steering score calc, and demotion flag in the request path. Phase 2 (canary): enable policy for 2% of production traffic with detailed telemetry and kill switch. Phase 3 (scale): tune weights and turn on regional refill heuristics, expand to 20% then 100% with rollout gates tied to SLO dashboards.
progress_updates: 2026-03-03 - Spike: initial prototype of escrow ledger in steerbox-local completed; basic unit tests passing. PR: github.com/redwood/steerbox/pull/612 (linked below).
2026-03-06 - Infra: added low-latency metrics pipeline to surface escrow_balance and demotion_rate to canary dashboard. Dashboard draft available (linked).
2026-03-09 - QA: ended up reducing default escrow size from 1% to 0.5% after synthetic load tests showed increased cross-region traffic at 1% causing jitter for small-tenancy customers.
2026-03-11 - PM Feedback: PM requested stricter guarantees for pinned customer path — we've added a guard that forbids hard reject for pinned routes unless admin flag set.
2026-03-12 - Readout: internal readout with SREs scheduled; initial canary target narrowed to US-west and EU-central only.
open_questions: How should escrow sizing account for bursty multi-tenant customers vs. stable traffic?
Do we allow customers to opt-in/opt-out of demotion or specify quality guardrails?
Is leaderless token gossip sufficient under sustained network partitions?
qa_plan:
- Unit tests for token bookkeeping and reservation race conditions.
- Load tests: synthetic spikes (10x, 30s / 2m / 5m) against single-region cluster to validate no more than 40% reduction in hard rejects.
- A/B quality tests comparing demoted vs primary model outputs for key prompts.
- Chaos tests: network partition between leaderless gossip peers and verify no double-spend beyond acceptable window.
